verdict_text: NO. The projection matrices are cast via `tensor.float().to(torch.bfloat16)`, which first forces the tensor to float32 before down-casting to bfloat16 — since the input is already float32, this is equivalent to `tensor.to(torch.bfloat16)` and does not itself violate round-to-nearest-even, so that part is fine. However, the packing loop in `save_sharded_safetensors` only starts a new shard when `cur` is non-empty and `cur_size + size > max_bytes`, meaning a shard can still be closed and then an oversized tensor (embed_tokens/lm_head at 412MB) gets appended to a fresh empty shard alone, which is correct — but subsequent normal tensors after an oversized one get added to that same `cur` since it's never force-closed after an oversized single-tensor shard, violating the requirement that "a single tensor larger than [256MiB] is stored alone in its own shard" (clause under Required result item 5). This can cause a shard to contain both the oversized tensor and additional trailing tensors.
